upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm inquiring about my child - I have one child, Alex, who's 14 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

**Are you responsible for Alex? That is, do you live with Alex and are you the main person looking after them (providing for their care, food, clothing, etc.)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am responsible for Alex. They live with me and I'm the main person looking after them - I provide for their care, food, clothing, all of that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. 

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently living in the UK - I live abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Since you're living abroad, I need to understand your situation better as this affects eligibility.

**Can you tell me which country you're currently living in, and whether you or your partner work in the UK or for a UK employer, or have any connection to the UK's social security system (such as paying National Insurance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living in Spain at the moment. No, neither my partner nor I work in the UK or for a UK employer, and we don't have any connection to the UK's social security system - we're not paying National Insurance or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have a few more questions to fully assess your situation.

**Are you or your partner a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of HM Forces), or working for an international organization, or an EU/EEA national working in another EU/EEA country?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of us are Crown servants, diplomats, or members of HM Forces. We're not working for an international organization either, and we're not EU/EEA nationals working in another EU/EEA country.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Just to make sure I have a complete picture:

**Are you or have you recently been subject to UK immigration control, or are there any other special circumstances about your residence status that I should know about? Also, have you been receiving Child Benefit in the past that has continued while you moved abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we're not subject to UK immigration control and there aren't any special circumstances about our residence status. And no, I haven't been receiving Child Benefit in the past - this is a new inquiry, I haven't been claiming it before.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for answering all of those questions. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Decision

Based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: While you are responsible for Alex (who is 14 years old) and they live with you, Child Benefit has a residence requirement. To be eligible, you generally must either be living in the UK or have a qualifying connection to the UK, such as:
- Being a Crown servant (diplomat, member of HM Forces, etc.)
- Working in the UK or paying UK National Insurance
- Being covered by certain EU coordination rules

Since you're living in Spain and neither you nor your partner work in the UK, pay UK National Insurance, are Crown servants, or are covered by applicable EU coordination provisions, you don't meet the residence requirements for Child Benefit.

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if you return to live in the UK), you may wish to inquire again at that time.
